hints.title: List the ways to make degree three
hints.body: In (1+2x+3x2)6, x3 comes either from three 2x terms or from one 2x term and one 3x2 term.
hints.recap: There are exactly two degree patterns.
hints.pitfall: Do not omit the mixed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> selection.
hints.pause: Count the placements for each pattern.

recall.reminder: Find every combination of powers that produces the requested degree.

hints.title: Count choices for each pattern
hints.body: For each power pattern, choose which brackets supply its nonconstant terms, then multiply by the numerical coefficients of those terms. Apply the same selection method to the other expansion.
hints.recap: The coefficient includes both the number of bracket choices and the coefficients of the chosen terms.
hints.pitfall: Choosing different term types is different from choosing several identical term types.
hints.pause: Calculate both requested coefficients and impose the stated factor-of-two relation.

recall.reminder: The coefficient includes both the number of bracket choices and the coefficients of the chosen terms.

solution:
The x3 coefficient in (1+2x+3x2)6 is (63)23+6·5·2·3=160+180=340. These are the three-linear-term and linear-plus-quadratic-term cases.

The x4 coefficient in (1−ax2)5 is (52)(−a)2=10a2. The given relation is 340=2(10a2), so a2=17 and a=±17.

Answer B.
knowledgePattern: Collect a coefficient through two multinomial selections
